scope: Thirteen previously held source expressions reconsidered under user instruction that ordinary but reusable language should be taught and only genuine one-time comparisons excluded. All remain hold-editorial at review time; no decision mutation.
selectedOwnerChecks: 2983 is distinct from selected 2324 emotional depth.
3307 needs a clear contrast with selected 1690 turn good intentions into daily habits.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Small choices give daily life its tone and texture.
rows.guideMeaning: The overall emotional quality and detail of life; sensory language used figuratively.
rows.reason: Reusable pair for the emotional quality and fine detail of experience. Teach it as a figurative evaluative pair, not a literal claim that daily life has touchable texture. Distinct from selected 2324 emotional depth, which concerns portrayal in a story.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Teenagers often resist the feeling of being managed.
rows.guideMeaning: The sense that another person is controlling one's decisions; a useful precise phrase.
rows.reason: Ordinary but precise and transferable across teenagers, staff or patients who feel their choices are being controlled. Differentiate actual management from the subjective feeling; do not infer bad intent.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Children often show their imagination out in the open.
rows.guideMeaning: Visible rather than hidden; a conventional phrase.
rows.reason: Conventional visibility phrase. The source imagination use is a little unusual, so original practice should give natural public/visible contexts without shifting to the narrower secret-disclosure sense.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Research needs more than careful bookkeeping.
rows.guideMeaning: Merely recording facts without creative insight; a business metaphor.
rows.reason: The phrase itself neutrally means accurate record-keeping; “merely recording facts without creative insight” arises from the whole sentence Research needs more than ..., not from careful bookkeeping alone. Author only if lesson keeps the neutral base sense and uses research as a contrast, otherwise retain hold.

rows.expression: build a world out of words
rows.exactGuideSentence: A skilled writer can build a world out of words.
rows.guideMeaning: Create a vivid fictional setting through language; a construction metaphor.
rows.recommendedTarget: build a world out of words
rows.reason: A reusable creative-writing construction for evoking a fictional setting in language. Transfer to different writing forms and avoid suggesting words literally make a physical world; not a one-time comparison exclusion.

rows.exactGuideSentence: They made a game out of almost nothing.
rows.guideMeaning: With very few resources or materials; a conventional phrase.
rows.reason: Reusable resource-scarcity phrase. Source game made with very few materials; transfer to other low-resource creative outcomes and distinguish almost nothing from literally nothing.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Her patience showed a quiet kind of strength during the delay.
rows.guideMeaning: A less visible but valuable personal capacity; strength is figurative.
rows.reason: Reusable evaluative phrase for understated resilience or patience. Teach that quiet means less visible, not less valuable; avoid equating it with passivity.

rows.expression: not everything worth having comes quickly
rows.exactGuideSentence: The course taught her that not everything worth having comes quickly.
rows.guideMeaning: Valuable results often require patience; a natural proverb-like pattern.
rows.recommendedTarget: not everything worth having comes quickly
rows.reason: Reusable proverb-like counsel about worthwhile outcomes requiring patience. Preserve its nonabsolute not everything wording; do not promise that patience always guarantees results.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Useful advice has to fit the person receiving it.
rows.guideMeaning: Guidance must suit someone's circumstances; a clothing-fit metaphor.
rows.reason: Use a full target such as advice/approach has to fit the person, grounded in Useful advice has to fit the person receiving it. Transfer suitability to a recipient’s circumstances; not a literal clothing fit.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The checklist helps us avoid the same trap again.
rows.guideMeaning: Repeat an avoidable mistake; a fixed trap metaphor.
rows.reason: The inventory label same trap again is clipped. Source sentence supplies a natural reusable full verb phrase The checklist helps us avoid the same trap again. Teach repeated avoidable error, not a literal trap.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Writers should pay attention to nuance in word choice.
rows.guideMeaning: Notice small differences in meaning or tone; a useful language-learning collocation.
rows.reason: Ordinary, reusable instructional collocation about small differences in meaning or tone. Lesson can assess recognition of nuance in word choice versus merely checking a dictionary definition; lack of idiom status is not a hold reason.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Without a calendar, life can become too reactive.
rows.guideMeaning: Daily action can be driven by emergencies rather than intention; a precise planning phrase.
rows.reason: A precise planning adjective: daily action driven by incoming demands rather than chosen priorities. Ground it in Without a calendar, life can become too reactive; distinguish responsiveness from excessive reactivity.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A written plan can turn vague intentions into clearer action.
rows.guideMeaning: A compact transformation pattern for planning; it makes the benefit concrete.
rows.recommendedTarget: turn vague intentions into clearer action
rows.reason: Inventory label is a fragment. Use the full source-bound clause A written plan can turn vague intentions into clearer action, with grammar allowing varied subjects; distinguish from selected 1690 turn good intentions into daily habits, which concerns sustained routine rather than planning specificity.

mutation: none; proposals only, no selected lessons or decisions edited
